title: Adaptive Linear Algebra
contribution: Extends the robust linear-algebra framework of S458 to adaptive (linear decision rule) solutions of linear systems and eigen-pairs, with closed-form SOCO/LO upper bounds and an exact cutting-plane method whose separation step is solved globally by RPT-BB, and reports smaller errors than robust and nominal solutions on synthetic multi-period and perturbed ill-conditioned systems.
problem_entry: {RO+LO; CP} Linear-algebra methods assume exact data and solutions independent of uncertain parameters (p. 1); S458's robust solution faces all perturbations with one x, while here x may adapt to revealed parameters such as past-period errors (pp. 1, 14); motivated by compressed sensing and static-equilibrium equations (p. 5); problem (2)/(5): min over decision rules of the worst-case residual (pp. 2, 6); eigen-pairs (22) (p. 17).
key_idea: Restrict solutions to linear decision rules x = u + V1 z + V2 vec(Z) or x = u + Vz (pp. 6-7); closed-form upper bounds by the triangle inequality and support functions (Theorems 1-4, pp. 6-10); exact solution by cutting planes with RPT-BB separation (Algorithm 1, pp. 12-13); multi-period systems adapt to past errors (Algorithm 2, p. 14); eigenvectors adapt under linear orthogonality conditions while the eigenvalues' adaptive part is zero at the optimum (pp. 18-19); all pairs by alternating optimization (Algorithm 3, p. 21).
assumptions: Data affine in (Z, z); Frobenius and l2 balls (U2), l1 sets (U1), polyhedral z, a budget set for eigen-pairs (pp. 6-7, 9, 19). Synthetic nearly singular matrices with sigma = 1e-14 or 1e-13 (pp. 15-16); A = A0'A0 with A0 of size (n-8) x n (p. 23); test perturbation = mean of 100 scenarios drawn from [0, 20], applied as A + diag(z-bar), far outside the training sets with rho, theta <= 1 (pp. 16, 23).
proof_devices: Triangle-inequality upper bounds for LDR min-max residuals, l2 and l1 versions (Theorems 1-2, pp. 6-7)
Robust convex optimization re-derivation of the bound, the gap read as the dropped rank-one constraints Q = wz' (Theorem 3, pp. 8-9)
Fixed-recourse LDR on dual variables for polyhedral sets (Theorem 4, pp. 9-10)
S-lemma reformulation of the squared problem, flagged nonconvex (Theorem 5, p. 11)
Cutting planes whose separation (a convex maximization over a ball) is solved globally by RPT-BB (Algorithm 1, pp. 12-13)
Condition-number argument via the block normal equations (A'A + rho I)[u, V] = [A'b, A'] (Theorem 6, pp. 13-14); [my reading] it covers the squared upper-bound problem only
Linear sufficient conditions for orthogonality of decision rules (Proposition 1, p. 18); four sign cases to avoid the zero solution (p. 20)
O(1/T) convergence of alternating optimization by citation (Theorem 9, p. 21); [my reading] sign-case selection and normalization are not block minimizations
experiments: Synthetic only. Multi-period (n = 100, 10 periods, 10 instances): ALS equals RLS for two periods, then has lower error (Fig. 1, p. 15). Perturbed systems: CLS errors of order 1e13-1e14, RLS 3.68-50.21, ALS lower; exact RPT-BB beats the bound clearly in two settings and does not run at n = 1000 (Table 1, p. 16). Eigen-pairs with n = 10: Ad-RPT best in all five settings by small margins, Ad-UB worse than nominal in three of five (Table 2, p. 23). No solver version, machine, times, variance or code (pp. 11, 15-16, 21, 23).
positioning: Extends the authors' own robust linear algebra (S458) with adaptive robust optimization and LDRs (Ben-Tal et al. 2004; Bertsimas and den Hertog 2022) and RPT-BB (S377); positions against Gaussian elimination, Krylov methods and perturbation theory, which 'does not allow for an exact solution in the presence of data uncertainty' (pp. 1-4, 24).
writing: Contributions list (p. 4); each theorem followed by a short proof; an unfilled running head and broken cross-references (pp. 2, 6, 9-10, 16, 19) mark an unfinished draft [my reading].
limits_future: Variables grow from O(n) to O(n^2), a diagonal V restores O(n) (p. 14); RPT-BB scales to hundreds of variables, the bound to thousands (p. 16); all eigen-pairs come from alternating optimization (p. 21). Future work only in general terms: real-world applications (p. 24).

method_links.note: Adaptive linear systems and eigen-pairs stay SOCO or LO in every bound and sub-problem except a flagged nonconvex S-lemma form; the boundary is printed as O(n^2) variables and as RPT-BB's reach (hundreds of variables) against the bound's (thousands).

Cheap bound and exact cutting-plane solution reported side by side, a certificate-like comparison; but dueled only against the nominal method and the authors' own robust solution, with no times, versions or machine.
rho and theta vary over a small hand-set grid; no curve and no bound tying the knob to protection; the price of adaptivity is stated in problem size, not objective.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: adaptive sequel of one's own robust formulation
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Extends the authors' robust linear algebra (S458) by letting solutions be affine functions of revealed parameters; confirms the abstract-level inference of card a3-04.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: exact optimum on a small solvable instance as the certificate for a heuristic
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Exact RPT-BB solutions at n <= 100 show where the closed-form upper bound is tight; only the bound reaches n = 1000.

transferable: Bound a min-max residual under a linear decision rule by splitting the norm with the triangle inequality: each uncertain block contributes its set radius times a Frobenius norm, giving a convex SOCO bound in closed form (Theorems 1-2, pp. 6-7).
Make a cutting-plane method exact when its separation step maximizes a convex function: replace the function by its biconjugate and solve globally by RPT-BB (pp. 12-13).
Keep orthogonality between decision rules linear by imposing the coefficient-wise sufficient conditions u'u_j = 0, V_j'u + V'u_j = 0, V'V_j = O (Proposition 1, p. 18).
Avoid the zero solution without nonconvex constraints: solve four sign cases with the linear constraints sum(u) >= delta or <= -delta (and likewise for V), then keep the best (p. 20).

quotes.text: we observe that the upper bound for ALS is in general tight, however there exist instances where the exact solution obtained by cutting planes and RPT-BB is significantly better
Finally, we note that RPT-BB scales to problems with variables in the hundreds, while the upper bound scales to problems with variables in the thousands

title: Stochastic and Dynamic Vehicle Routing in the Euclidean Plane: The Multiple-Server, Capacitated Vehicle Case. 1990
contribution: Extends the authors' dynamic traveling repairman problem to m vehicles and capacity q: heavy-traffic system time falls as 1/m^2, independent partitioning keeps single-server constant factors, and capacity adds a radial-collection term that makes stability depend on geometry and the median the optimal depot; it adds extensions to d dimensions and general densities, and asymptotic models for fleet sizing, districting and the travel-waiting trade-off.
problem_entry: {SD; AP motivation} Static, deterministic VRPs are 'not always appropriate' as models of practice, and delivery time is often the better objective (p. 5); rolling horizons are 'inherently ad hoc' (p. 6); their own single uncapacitated vehicle is 'somewhat unrealistic for most practical purposes' (p. 10). Problem: policies minimizing expected system time for m vehicles from m depots, with at most q demands per tour (p. 10).
key_idea: Keep the bracket of lower bounds over all policies and constant-factor policies (pp. 8-10). m servers: a 1/m^2 reduction (p. 3); randomized assignment's factor grows like m (p. 18), the G/G/m TSP policy's like (m+1)/2 (p. 21); independent partitioning keeps any single-server constant (pp. 21-22). Capacity: radial collection cost in the stability condition (pp. 11, 24-25), qTSP and qG/G/m policies (pp. 25-29), median optimal as depot (Theorems 4-5, pp. 28-29). Extensions to d dimensions and general densities (pp. 31-33); strategic models (pp. 33-38).
assumptions: Poisson arrivals, uniform locations in a bounded convex region with piecewise-linear boundary, general on-site service with finite first and second moments, constant speed (p. 8); limits assumed to exist (p. 12); exactly q demands per tour (p. 22); subregions reasonably similar and compact (p. 21); identical Voronoi cells and m = kp for multi-depot policies (pp. 28-31). No data.
proof_devices: m-median relaxation for the light-traffic bound (Theorem 1, p. 13); mSQM asymptotically optimal (p. 17)
Tagged-demand argument with Wald's equation and Markov's inequality (Lemma 1, pp. 14-16)
Stochastic dominance from the Haimovich-Magnanti k-median result (Lemma 2, pp. 15-16), giving gamma ~ 0.153 (p. 16)
Two random points on a tour: two radial legs plus the hops between them lower-bound the tour length (Theorem 3, Lemma 3, pp. 23-24); the factor 1/3 called a by-product of the proof (p. 24)
Kingman's G/G/m heavy-traffic limit plus TSP asymptotics, with the set size rewritten as the travel ratio y (pp. 18-21, 27)
Independent partitioning scales area and arrival rate by 1/m (pp. 21-22)
Depot-location theorem by contradiction: the lower bound blows up while the qTSP upper bound stays finite (Theorem 4, p. 28)
experiments: No new simulation; reuses the predecessor's simulated constants (SFC ~ 0.66, NN ~ 0.64; pp. 9-10). One illustration: y* = 0.906 gives T = 578, and 10% less travel per demand (y = 0.81) raises T by 21% to 702 (Fig. 2, p. 37). The claim about SFC and NN travel rests on simulations not shown (p. 38).
positioning: Against static VRP and rolling-horizon practice (pp. 5-6); related work: TRP, PTSP/PVRP (his own thesis line), the stochastic queue median, polling and machine-repairman models, Psaraftis's DTSP (pp. 6-8); builds on reference [12], which is S016 (pp. 8, 40).
writing: Recaps the predecessor's results as the base (pp. 8-10), gives each bound term a physical reading such as the radial collection cost (p. 11), and judges its own results candidly ('undesirable', p. 18; 'somewhat unsatisfactory', p. 21); conjectures are labelled as such (pp. 22, 33).
limits_future: Open: Conjecture 1 on partitioned optimal policies (p. 22); Conjecture 2 for nonuniform demand (p. 33); the constant gap needs 'a new approach to the proof of Lemma 1'; networks instead of the Euclidean metric (p. 39); asymmetric depots need better bounds (p. 31). Against card S032: gamma ~ 0.153 here (p. 16) vs 0.266 there; a convex piecewise-linear region here (p. 8) vs boundedness only; no wedge or D/G/m policies here (pp. 17-22); sections 4-5.2 not mentioned in card S032 (not checked).

method_links.note: Early form: one knob y (travel per demand relative to its critical value) indexes the travel-waiting trade-off, with a worked price (10% less travel, 21% more system time); radial costs flagged as not tradeable; nonparametric policies faulted for lacking the knob.
A model replaces ad hoc rolling horizons, and its asymptotic formulas serve as building blocks for normative planning; the class kept is an analysable queue, not LP or MIO.
Certificates are analytic lower bounds over all policies; open gaps are printed as conjectures, and the 1/3 factor is flagged as an artefact of the proof.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: lower bound over all policies, then constant-factor policies
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Light- and heavy-traffic lower bounds for m vehicles and capacity q, then the mSQM, RA, G/G/m, partitioning, qTSP and qG/G/m policies measured against them.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: print the looseness of your own constants and the conjecture that would close it
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The (m+1)/2 factor called somewhat unsatisfactory; the 1/3 factor a by-product of the proof; closing the constant gap needs a new proof of Lemma 1; Conjectures 1-2.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: carry deterministic devices into the stochastic version and measure what survives
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: TSP asymptotics, the Haimovich-Magnanti k-median dominance and the Haimovich-Rinnooy Kan radial collection cost carried into the dynamic model.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: asymptotic formulas as building blocks for strategic models
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: A closed-form fleet size from min c1 T(m) + c2 m; districting with areas proportional to vehicle speeds; the travel-waiting curve from the policy formula.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: working paper sharpened before the journal
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Here gamma ~ 0.153, a convex piecewise-linear region and no wedge or D/G/m policies; card S032 (the 1993 journal version) has gamma ~ 0.266, boundedness only and both policies.

transferable: Lower-bound a dynamic routing policy with a tagged demand: travel to it is at least the minimum distance from the locations that could precede it (queue, servers, arrivals during its wait); bound that minimum with Wald's equation and a stochastic-dominance lemma, then substitute into the stability condition (pp. 14-16).
Lift single-server guarantees to m servers by independent partitioning: area and arrival rate both scale by 1/m, so the constant factor is unchanged (pp. 21-22).
Lower-bound the length of a capacitated tour by two radial legs to random points of the tour plus the hops between them (pp. 23-24).

Rewrite a policy's tuning parameter as the ratio of a cost to its critical value; in heavy traffic the optimum then sits near 1, and the curve becomes the decision-maker's trade-off (pp. 20-21, 36-37).
coauthors: Garrett van Ryzin (MIT Operations Research Center)

quotes.text: This appears to be just a by-product of the randomization used in the proof rather than a fundamental characteristic of the capacitated case.

Although these policies have advantages for systems where exact parameter estimation is difficult or parameters change frequently, this lack of travel/waiting cost control should be considered a disadvantage.

title: Signed Budget Uncertainty for Robust Mixed-Integer Optimization
contribution: Introduces signed and laminar signed budget uncertainty for robust MIO with binary uncertainty-affected variables, with compact robust counterparts (two extra variables and two constraints per uncertain constraint; 4K - 2K_L for laminar families), a 2^K nominal-problem alternative, set constructions from the CLT and hierarchical forecasts, and experiments showing large speed-ups over the standard RC and optima that no re-tuning of the classical budget Gamma reproduces.
problem_entry: {RO+IO} Classical budgets bound aggregate absolute deviations, but applications often hold signed aggregate information: regional demand or population forecasts, CLT bounds, hierarchies (p. 2); earlier tractability results with signed aggregates cover objective uncertainty and specific applications (p. 3). Problem (1): MIO with binary uncertainty-affected variables and an uncertain constraint matrix in a (laminar) signed budget set (pp. 4-5, 8-9).
key_idea: Closed-form worst case (a+)'x + min{0, a+_P - sum_j(a+_j x_j + a-_j (1 - x_j))} (Theorem 1, p. 6), linearized with one binary variable, one continuous variable and two constraints, M = 2 sum eta_j (p. 7); one uncertain constraint = two nominal problems (Corollary 1, p. 7); laminar recursion with corrections w <= 0 and u >= 0 (Theorem 2, pp. 9-10), or 2^K nominal problems (Corollary 2, p. 11); sets from the CLT, stable laws and reconciled hierarchical forecasts (pp. 11-13).
assumptions: c, d, B, beta deterministic; objective uncertainty moved into the constraints by an epigraph; uncertainty in B, beta independent of A's (p. 5); constraint-wise robustness; nonempty sets with tightened aggregate bounds (pp. 5, 9); compactness needs linear dependence, binary variables and a laminar structure (p. 17). Synthetic maximum coverage with the total population fixed (eta_P = 0) and 5% / 1% laminar widths (p. 14); knapsack with n1 = 192 and 5% widths (p. 16); [my reading] the data constructions of section 4 are not used in section 5.
proof_devices: LP duality for the standard RC with 2 + 2n1 extra variables, or 2K + 2n1 for laminar sets (Appendix A; pp. 6, 9, 17-19)
Split the indices by x_j = 1 or 0: the worst case is a min of two expressions, with attainment by the intermediate value theorem (Theorem 1; pp. 6, 20-21)
Big-M linearization of the min with M = 2 sum eta_j (p. 7)
Robust feasible set as the union of two nominal feasible sets (Corollary 1, p. 7); 2^K nominal problems for laminar families (Corollary 2, p. 11)
Recursive worst case over the laminar tree with downward and upward corrections (Theorem 2, pp. 9-10; proofs in Appendix C not read)
CLT and stable-law aggregate bounds mu(P) +- C sigma(P) (pp. 11-12); MinT forecast reconciliation for coherent intervals (p. 13; example pp. 34-36)
experiments: Python, Gurobi 12.0.1, i5-10600KF, 32 GB, code on GitHub (p. 13). Maximum coverage with n1 = 100-10,000, 5 instances and a 1-h limit: the standard RC hits the limit from n1 = 500, the compact signed RC stays near nominal to n1 = 5000 (Table 1, p. 14); Gurobi min/max constraints beat big-M (p. 15). A Gamma grid recovers the signed optimum only at n1 in {100, 500, 1000} with gamma <= 0.3, and more slowly (Table 2, p. 15). Knapsack: enumeration competitive for K <= 4, fails within 1 h for K >= 24, compact RC under 1 s (p. 16). [my reading] Table 1 averages exclude time-limit instances, and flattened superscripts show limit hits at n1 = 10,000 (p. 14).
positioning: Extends the Bertsimas-Sim (2004) budgets; inspired by Kerkkamp (2014); extends Goerigk-Lendl (2021) and Yaman (2023) from objective to constraint uncertainty; data constructions after Bandi-Bertsimas (2012) and hierarchical forecasting (Athanasopoulos et al. 2024) (pp. 2-4, 11-13).
writing: The abstract gives counts (two variables, two constraints) and the claim that Gamma tuning cannot reproduce the solutions (p. 1); an intuition paragraph after each theorem (pp. 6, 9-10); a numeric example of model size (p. 10).
limits_future: Compactness relies on linear dependence, binary variables and the laminar structure (p. 17); enumeration grows costly with K (pp. 3, 16). Future: structural conditions for compact RCs, general integer or continuous variables, nonlinear RO, non-laminar aggregates (p. 17). [my reading] No out-of-sample or simulated-violation evaluation (pp. 13-16).

method_links.note: Signed and laminar budgets keep MIO with a constant extra size per uncertain constraint; the nominal-solve route mirrors step 3's n + 1 nominal solves; the boundary is printed (three conditions for compactness; enumeration fails at K >= 24).

The lever is the set's shape, not Gamma's level: re-tuning Gamma cannot reach the signed optima; section 4 sets aggregate widths from data (CLT, forecasts), as the correction asks, but the experiments fix them by hand.

The reporting half of the protocol is present (solver version, machine, 1-h limit, counts of time-limit hits, public code); there is no warm start or heuristic incumbent, and the duel is against the standard RC and the classical budget set.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: practitioners' maxims encoded as uncertainty-set geometry
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Net forecasts by region, province or category become signed, laminar budgets; reconciled hierarchical forecasts supply coherent widths.
CLT bounds mu(P) +- C sigma(P) and stable-law bounds define the aggregate constraints, after Bandi-Bertsimas (2012).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: subsume the incumbent as a special case
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The objective-uncertainty results of Goerigk-Lendl and Yaman become special cases of the constraint-uncertainty results, with the objective moved into the constraints by an epigraph.

transferable: With binary uncertainty-affected variables, split the indices by the value of x_j: the worst case becomes the min of two deterministic expressions (or a recursion over K sets), linearized with one binary variable (pp. 6-7, 9-10).

When the worst case is a min of deterministic expressions and only one constraint is uncertain, solve the robust problem as nominal problems with the nominal problem's specialized algorithm, for example knapsack dynamic programming (pp. 7, 11).
Test whether a new uncertainty set is a re-tuning of the old one: solve the classical model over a grid of Gamma and score each solution under the new set (Table 2, p. 15).
Build aggregate bounds from data with the CLT per set (mu +- 2 sigma or 3 sigma) or from reconciled hierarchical forecasts (pp. 11-13).
coauthors: Danique de Moor (MIT Sloan), Dick den Hertog (Amsterdam Business School), Federica Donnini (University of Florence)

quotes.text: Only for a few instances and carefully chosen values of Γ is the signed budget optimum recovered.

In this paper, compactness relies on the linear dependence on the uncertain parameters, the binary nature of the uncertainty-affected decision variables, and, in the hierarchical setting, the laminar structure of the aggregate sets.

title: Distributionally Robust Optimization with General Uncertainty Structure
contribution: Gives an exact framework for moment- and confidence-set DRO beyond max-of-affine functions: DRO is rewritten as RO and solved globally by a cutting-set algorithm with RPT-BB (convex and SLC dependence, the latter under a new weakly nested linear ambiguity set) or by a conic reformulation (concave dependence); it is used to audit LDR bounds on appointment-scheduling instances and to solve a mixed-integer conic capital-budgeting problem.
problem_entry: {RO+CP; IO} Exact results for moment- and confidence-set DRO (WKS 2014) need max-of-affine functions and strictly nested confidence sets (pp. 2-3); the accuracy of approximations 'is difficult to assess' because the optimum is unknown (p. 3); moment sets suit small-sample, expert-driven and regulatory settings (p. 2). Problem (1): min c'x s.t. worst-case expectation of v(x, z) <= tau, v convex in x (p. 5).
key_idea: Theorem 1 (from WKS): the DRO constraint equals robust constraints over the disjoint regions induced by nesting (p. 8). Convex dependence: biconjugate reformulation plus cutting sets with RPT-BB separation (pp. 9-12). SLC dependence: a new NL set with weak nesting, whose regions split into at most prod R_k convex pieces (Lemma 1, p. 13; Theorem 3, p. 14). Concave dependence: the point mass at the mean when feasible (Theorem 4, p. 16); otherwise support function plus concave conjugate gives a conic counterpart (Theorem 5, pp. 16-18).
assumptions: NG: E[Az] = b, conic confidence sets with probability bounds, strict nesting (A1)-(A3) (p. 6); NL: support intersected with polyhedra, weak nesting (A3*) (p. 7); v Lipschitz in x and mild regularity for convergence (p. 10; Appendix C not read); the two-stage adaptive extension is claimed without derivation (pp. 5-6) [my reading]. Data: BSZ's ASP instances 3-4 and N = 8-20 (pp. 21-22); a budget threshold holding with probability >= 0.9 (p. 23); capital budgeting with N = 12, T = 5 from Wang et al. (2025) and an event probability in [0.65, 0.75] (pp. 25-26).
proof_devices: Moment-problem duality restated from WKS, turning DRO into robust constraints over disjoint regions (Theorem 1, p. 8; proof in Appendix B not read)
Biconjugate reformulation making the robust constraint bilinear in the uncertainty (Theorem 2, pp. 9-10)

Cutting-set algorithm with RPT lifting V = wz', pairwise constraint products, candidate scenarios V*_s/w*_s as lower bounds, and branching on the top eigenvector of the deviation from rank one (pp. 10-12)
Region decomposition by one violated inequality per child set (Lemma 1, p. 13)
Jensen's inequality: the point mass at the mean is the worst case for concave dependence (Theorem 4, p. 16)
Fenchel duality with support functions and concave conjugates (Theorem 5, pp. 16-18); power-cone representation of the NPV conjugate (Corollary 3, pp. 24-25)
experiments: Julia 1.12.2, Gurobi 12.0.3, MOSEK 11.0.30, i7-1165G7, 16 GB; code on request (p. 18). ASP against BSZ (Table 4, p. 22): Mean and Mean-MM optima equal BSZ's bounds; for PCM-alpha (0 < alpha < 1) the exact optima exceed BSZ's upper bounds by up to 1.54%, footnoted as unexplained (p. 21); for PCM-0 the LDR is conservative by 6.74% and 2.76%; up to 710 s. N = 8-20: 23 s to 4,139 s (Table 5, p. 22). NL lies between the support-only and support-plus-budget sets (Table 6, p. 23). Capital budgeting: the worst-case NPV improves monotonically with event constraints, under 1.2 s, same portfolio (Table 7, p. 26).
positioning: Extends Wiesemann-Kuhn-Sim (2014) beyond max-of-affine functions and strict nesting; uses RPT-BB (S377, S708, S415) and Ben-Tal-den Hertog-Vial (2015); contrasts with Wasserstein and phi-divergence DRO (pp. 2-3); audits his own BSZ 2019 paper (S028) (pp. 21-22).
writing: Table 1 maps function class x ambiguity set x method (p. 4); contributions in two bullets (p. 4); a concrete limitations paragraph (p. 27); corresponding author Brugman (p. 1).
limits_future: Lifted RPT reformulations grow quadratically in the uncertainty dimension; NL needs linear confidence sets, excluding ellipsoids; the NL and capital-budgeting experiments are illustrations (pp. 23, 25-27). Future: benchmark LDR, SAA and SDP approximations against exact values; multistage settings (p. 27).

method_links.note: DRO is rewritten exactly as RO; the ambiguity set is redesigned (NL, weak nesting) to keep tractability; the concave case stays conic, or mixed-integer conic with binaries; the boundary is printed (quadratic growth of the lifted RPT, linear confidence sets only).
An exact global solve (epsilon = 0.01) audits an approximation (the LDR bounds of his 2019 BSZ paper) instead of dueling a greedy heuristic; versions, machine and times stated, code only on request.

The property priced is information: the worst-case value against the number of event constraints, and support-only >= NL >= support-plus-budget in conservatism; the levels (0.9; [0.65, 0.75]) are fixed by hand.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: tightness audit of one's own bound
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Re-solves the ASP instances of his 2019 BSZ paper (S028): bounds tight for Mean and Mean-MM, LDR conservative for PCM-0 (6.74%, 2.76%), and reported bounds below the exact optimum for PCM-alpha, footnoted as unexplained.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: exact optimum on a small solvable instance as the certificate for a heuristic
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Exact solutions for N <= 20 serve as reference values for approximation-based DRO (LDR, SAA, SDP).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: subsume the incumbent as a special case
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: WKS's max-of-affine case falls inside the SLC class, and Table 1 places it as one row of the framework.

transferable: When an exact reformulation needs strictly nested sets, redefine the sets by linear inequalities that may share boundaries, split each nonconvex region into convex pieces by choosing one violated inequality per child set, and generate the pieces lazily (pp. 13-14).
Before building a DRO model concave in the uncertainty, check whether the point mass at the mean is feasible: if so, the worst case is the nominal problem at the mean (Theorem 4, p. 16).
Write a concave robust constraint with the set's support function and the function's concave conjugate, so that either can change without re-deriving the other (pp. 17-18).
Use the exact solver to re-solve a published paper's instances and report the gap per ambiguity set, with a footnote on what could not be checked (Table 4 and footnote 1, pp. 21-22).
coauthors: Judith Brugman (Tilburg University; corresponding author), Dick den Hertog (Amsterdam Business School), Johan S. H. van Leeuwaarden (Tilburg University)

quotes.text: our optimal objective values are slightly higher than the bounds reported in BSZ (deviating more than 1%), which suggests that the bounds may be numerically inaccurate

First, scalability is limited by the size of the lifted RPT reformulations, which grow quadratically in the uncertainty dimension and can become computationally demanding for larger instances or many confidence or decomposition regions.

title: Predicting Concurrence of Heatwaves, Droughts, and Wildfires with Spatiotemporal Deep Learning
contribution: Proposes a multi-task spatiotemporal deep-learning benchmark on FireCube (Greece, 2009-2020) to predict heatwaves, drought severity and wildfire occurrence jointly, with climate-zone-specific indicators and a variance-normalized multi-task loss; only preliminary ConvGRU training curves are reported.
problem_entry: {ML; AP} Compound heat, drought and fire extremes amplify impacts, but single-hazard forecasts ignore their interactions and multi-task learning has not treated the three together (p. 1); hypothesis: a joint spatiotemporal model beats separate models, especially for compound risks (p. 1).
key_idea: A shared encoder with task-specific heads for a heatwave indicator, SPEI drought severity and burned-area probability (p. 2); baselines ConvGRU, ConvLSTM, Earthformer and Time-SSM (pp. 2-3); summer-aggregated targets for policy time-frames (p. 2).
assumptions: FireCube, 1 km x 1 km x 1 day, 19 features (p. 3); a zone-specific heatwave threshold (three days above the 90th percentile), SPEI from an 8-day water balance with a generalized logistic fit, wildfire from burned-area polygons (p. 2); a chronological split, training to September 2018 and validation through September 2020 (p. 3).
proof_devices: n/a (no formulation or proofs); the loss is a variance-normalized sum of per-task MSEs (p. 3)
experiments: None yet: ConvGRU losses decrease across the tasks, with difficulty on rare events (p. 3). [my reading] All baselines are multi-task, so no single-task comparator tests the hypothesis, and no compound-event metric is defined (pp. 1-3).
positioning: Against single-hazard wildfire, drought and heatwave models; builds on multi-task learning in climate science (Ling et al. 2022; Sadler et al. 2022) and on the FireCube data (Prapas et al.) (pp. 1-3).
writing: Proposal voice ('we aim', 'we plan'), an explicit hypothesis (p. 1) and a pathway-to-impact section (pp. 3-4).
limits_future: A planned data set, benchmark and public release of data and code (pp. 1, 4); limitations mentioned only generically (p. 4); extension to other regions and hazards (pp. 3-4).

method_links.note: Scored by prediction error only; decisions (early warning, irrigation, land management) appear only in the impact section, with no owner, decision or current rule; a proposal on which he is third author.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: sponsor-and-edit senior authorship on student-led lines outside optimization
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Third of four authors on a deep-learning proposal with no optimization model, with another author corresponding; whether the line is student-led is not stated.

transferable: In a multi-task loss that mixes a sparse binary target with continuous targets, normalize each task's MSE by its baseline variance before summing, so the sparse task is not swamped (p. 3).
Define extreme-event labels relative to climate zones (zone-specific percentiles and SPEI fits) rather than with one global threshold (p. 2).
coauthors: Ana Trišović (MIT; corresponding author), Gabe Miller (MIT), Jie K. Hu (The Ohio State University)

quotes.text: To balance task disparities (e.g., sparse wildfires vs. continuous drought indicators), each MSE term is normalized by baseline variance before summing, preventing any single task from dominating gradient updates.
The ConvGRU baseline shows promise in preliminary results, with training and validation losses steadily decreasing across all three tasks.

title: Optimized Oversampling
contribution: Proposes Optimized-Oversampling (O2), which generates synthetic minority points by maximizing a trained classifier's minority probability over its input, with diversity terms and a filtering classifier, and reports AUC and F1 ranks on par with or better than SMOTE variants for CART and LR on 16 data sets, and weaker results with RF.
problem_entry: {ML} Imbalanced data degrade classifiers (pp. 1-2); more than 85 SMOTE extensions exist, and deep generative oversamplers add cost without significant gains (pp. 2-3); SMOTE is randomized (pp. 2, 11).
key_idea: Maximize g_w(z) plus distance rewards to earlier synthetic points and to the original minority points, minus an l2 term (problem (2), pp. 3-4); a CART version with the leaf splits as linear constraints (problem (5), p. 7); a TabNet filter (p. 7); multi-target imputation of categorical features (Algorithm 2, pp. 8-9); other methods' points as warm starts (pp. 12-13).
assumptions: 16 public data sets, n 583-245,056, imbalance ratio 0.02-0.33 (Table 1, p. 10); CART, LR and RF from scikit-learn, XGBoost excluded (p. 10); lambda1 = 0.1, lambda2 = 0.05, lambda3 = 0.1 fixed, L-BFGS started from minority points (p. 11); the text says 14 data sets (p. 8) against 16 (pp. 1, 10) [my reading].
proof_devices: Lipschitz-gradient argument giving stationarity of limit points for gradient-related methods (Theorem 1, p. 5)
Sigmoid Lipschitz bound giving L = ||w||^2 for LR (pp. 5-6)

[my reading] As written, the coefficient of ||z||^2 in (2) is lambda1 (k-1)/k + lambda2 - lambda3, positive for k >= 3 with the fixed lambdas (pp. 4, 11), so the maximization is unbounded; the SVM objective sgn(w'z) has zero gradient almost everywhere (p. 6)
experiments: Per method and ratio, 10 oversampled copies x 35 seeds; 5-10 ratios; the best ratio reported, chosen on test AUC (p. 11). O2 is first in AUC on CART and LR and fifth on RF; first in F1 on CART, second on LR, fourth on RF (p. 3; Tables 2-7, pp. 12-14); LR average F1 is 56.2 against SMOTE's 61.9 (Table 5, p. 13). LoRAS warm starts help in five of nine rows, which the text calls five of eight (pp. 12, 14); filtering helps, with p-values (Table 9, p. 15). No run times.
positioning: Against SMOTE and its many extensions (Kovacs 2019), deep generative oversamplers and cost-sensitive learning (pp. 2-3); baselines chosen as in LoRAS (p. 3); OCTs named as an alternative generator (p. 7).
writing: Determinism claimed in the abstract, the contributions and the conclusion (pp. 1, 3, 16); results stated as ranks (p. 3); an authors' contributions statement gives Bertsimas the overall supervision (p. 17).
limits_future: Weaker with RF (pp. 3, 16); data sets with only categorical features excluded (p. 9); no future work. [my reading] The determinism claim conflicts with the reported L-BFGS randomness (p. 11) and with the Table 8 label (p. 14).

method_links.note: A duel against the SMOTE family on 16 data sets and three learners with released code, and rival methods' points as warm starts (LoRAS); but no run times, no certificate (stationary points only), and the ratio selected on the test metric for all methods.
A preprocessing heuristic is recast as optimization over a trained model's input, but the class kept is a generic smooth NLP solved to stationarity, or linear leaf constraints for CART.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: optimize the training sample, not the model
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The learners stay unchanged; synthetic minority points are generated by optimization and filtered; confirms the abstract-level link of card a3-05.

transferable: Generate synthetic minority points by gradient ascent on a trained classifier's minority probability, with distance terms to spread the points, an l2 term and a second classifier as a filter (pp. 4-7); [my reading] check that the l2 weight exceeds the combined distance weights, or the problem is unbounded.
For tree models, turn the leaves where the minority is predicted with high probability into linear constraints and place the synthetic points inside them (p. 7).
Use a rival method's synthetic points as warm starts, so that the optimizer improves them rather than replaces them (pp. 12-13).
coauthors: Thodoris Koukouvinos, Angelos Georgios Koulouras (MIT Operations Research Center)

quotes.text: By solving such optimization problems again and again, we can generate multiple points that are likely to belong to the minority class as specified by some model and thereby balance the dataset.
In our method, the randomness comes mainly from the way L-BFGS operates.

title: Imbalanced classification via robust optimization
contribution: Trains LR and SVM on the hardest balanced training subset chosen by robust optimization, dualized into one convex program, and reports F1 gains of 5.7-8.0% and AUC gains of 0.6-1.0% over weighted, IHT and GSMOTE baselines on 20 UCI data sets, at up to about 33 minutes for n = 58,000.
problem_entry: {ML+RO} Imbalance (an IR of 112 for pediatric ciTBI in his own study; about 100 in fraud) degrades classifiers (p. 2); weighting, oversampling and undersampling generate or delete data, add training time, overfit or lose information (pp. 1-2); RO classification so far addresses data uncertainty, not imbalance (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Binary indicators select floor(t n1) minority points and k floor(t n1) majority points; maximize the regularized log-likelihood under the hardest such balanced subset (problem (4), p. 4); the convex hull and LP duality give one concave program for LR (p. 5) and a convex QP for SVM (p. 7); a box around the weighted LR/SVM solution is added when the solution collapses to zero (pp. 5-8). [my reading] The inner minimum keeps the highest-loss points: an adversarial undersampling.
assumptions: Standardized features (p. 3); 20 UCI data sets, IR 3.7-33.7, n 79-245,056 (p. 9; Table 1, p. 11); baselines weighted LR/SVM, IHT and GSMOTE in scikit-learn, the robust method in JuMP with IPOPT (p. 9); baselines tuned on held-out validation F1 (weighted and IHT over 2 settings each, GSMOTE over 84), the robust method on in-sample F1 over 16 settings (pp. 8-10); the F1 threshold is not stated [my reading].
proof_devices: Convex hull of cardinality-constrained binary selections (p. 4)
LP duality on the inner selection problem, substituted back into a single concave maximization for LR (problems (7)-(8), p. 5) and a convex QP for SVM (problems (14)-(15), p. 7)
A proximity box |beta_k - beta-hat_k| <= delta around the weighted solution to rule out the zero solution (problems (9) and (16), pp. 5-8)
experiments: F1: LR +0.046 (8.0%) over weighted and +0.045 (7.8%) over GSMOTE; SVM +0.033 (5.7%) and +0.039 (6.8%) (p. 10). AUC +0.6-1.0% (p. 11). Per-set losses (e.g., libras-move 0.651 against 0.849) and win-loss-tie tables (Tables 1-7, pp. 11-15). Times on one Xeon core: robust LR takes 2,008 s at n = 58,000, against 0.48 s weighted and 391 s for GSMOTE (Table 5, p. 14). Five splits; no standard deviations or tests.
positioning: Against weighted learning, the SMOTE family (GSMOTE) and undersampling (IHT) (p. 2); earlier RO classification (Bertsimas et al. 2011; Pant et al. 2011; S104) handles data uncertainty, not imbalance (pp. 2-3); motivated by stable regression (S312) (p. 4).
writing: The abstract states the gain and its price in running time, with the scale (p. 1); absolute and relative gains in the results text (pp. 10-11); no limitations section (p. 13).
limits_future: None stated (p. 13). [my reading] The 'one to two orders of magnitude' slow-down (p. 13) holds against GSMOTE; against weighted LR, Table 5 shows three to four orders (p. 14); only the robust method is selected on in-sample F1 (pp. 8-9).

method_links.note: The combinatorial choice of the hardest balanced training subset is dualized away, so LR stays convex and SVM stays a QP; solve times are measured up to n = 58,000.

Duels weighted LR/SVM, IHT and GSMOTE on 20 data sets, with per-set losses, win-loss-tie tables and timings; the incumbent (weighted LR/SVM) is an anchor box, not a warm start; only the robust method is selected on in-sample F1, and its grid is larger than those of the weighted and IHT baselines; certificates are moot (convex problems).

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Following stable regression, the assignment of data to training and validation is optimized adversarially instead of randomized.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: incumbent-anchored box when the robust model degenerates
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: If the robust solution collapses to zero, a box |beta_k - beta-hat_k| <= delta around the weighted LR/SVM solution is added, with delta tuned by validation.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: optimize the training sample, not the model
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Variant: the model is trained on an adversarially selected subset (selection, not generation).

transferable: Replace a random train/validation split by an adversarial one: put cardinality-constrained selection indicators in an inner minimization that is linear in them, so that the convex hull and LP duality give one convex program (pp. 4-7).
When a robust model degenerates to the zero solution, constrain it to a small box around the incumbent's solution and tune the box width (pp. 5-6, 8).
Report pairwise wins, losses and ties against each baseline next to the averages, and a timing table that prints the price (Tables 5-7, pp. 14-15).

quotes.text: Under our robust framework, the training set represents the hardest set among the given data.
For LR, the robust method slows down computation by one to two orders of magnitude, which is caused by solving a constrained convex optimization problem.
